audit_methodology.pass_1_static_probe: line-by-line review of src/, src-tauri/, scripts/, .github/workflows/, tests/, test_documents/, phase_2_report.json
audit_methodology.pass_2_lifecycle_simulation: real subprocess execution probes: 08_hybrid_pdf.pdf image extraction in space/non-space paths, 03_persian_rtl_document.pdf glyph extraction, 06_complex_tables.pdf table recognition, pandoc GFM round-trip with $PATH inline code, pandoc Persian UTF-8 round-trip, Windows reserved filename creation
audit_methodology.pass_3_adversarial_verification: each finding cross-checked against actual measured output or code path; no string-matching assertions

known_vulnerabilities_audit.code_location: build-windows job steps (rust-cache@v2 with cache-on-failure=false, shared-key tauri-v2-windows-release-v2) and [profile.release] (codegen-units=16, lto=false)
known_vulnerabilities_audit.root_cause_analysis: The +79.6% figure (167s vs 300s) is statistically invalid: it compares the single best Phase 1.5 run against the single worst Phase 2 run. Measured run history: Phase 1.5 stable runs 167/243/236s (median 236), Phase 2 runs 240/300/194s (median 240). Median is flat. The build-windows job is byte-identical between phases (git diff d1b7453..94e9c23 shows only quality-job changes: added pip install pymupdf4llm and apt pandoc, which run in parallel off the critical path, 19s->44-58s). Identical docs-only jobs in Phase 2 measured 296s and 189s, a 56% spread proving runner/cache noise dominates. Real structural contributors: (1) cache-on-failure=false (enforced by refinement_check.py) means the two failed Phase 2 runs (5eeccdd, 5b22481) skipped cache saves, forcing 94e9c23 to restore a stale cache and partially recompile; (2) new Rust modules (conversion.rs ~450 lines) add a few seconds of compile; (3) shared windows-latest runner contention is unbounded.
known_vulnerabilities_audit.architectural_impact: The under-3-minute CI budget is violated in worst-case runs; extremes are recorded as 'regressions' in reports, eroding gate credibility; every docs-only push burns 3-5 minutes of runner time.
known_vulnerabilities_audit.remediation_strategy: Report median-of-3 instead of extremes; add a secondary fallback cargo cache keyed by Cargo.lock hash (keep cache-on-failure=false as required by the refinement contract); give cargo test its own cache key so test builds never churn the release cache; document runner-noise variance in reports. No code/architecture change is required for the release profile - the regression is measurement methodology + cache resilience, not compilation strategy.

known_vulnerabilities_audit.root_cause_analysis: process_pdf invokes Command::output(), which blocks until the child exits and never retains the Child handle. cancel_batch only sets an AtomicBool and re-marks queued items; the worker polls the flag exclusively between items. There is no ChildProcess::kill() path anywhere: an in-flight Python/pymupdf4llm process is invisible to cancellation. Verified structurally: no Child handle exists after output() returns.
known_vulnerabilities_audit.architectural_impact: A corrupted or adversarial PDF (decompression bomb, pathological content stream) that hangs pymupdf4llm leaves the batch stuck forever in 'running' with one item 'processing'; user cancellation is a no-op; the subprocess buffers (stdout/stderr, growing markdown) are retained in memory for the hang duration; violates the 0% crash / robustness contract.
known_vulnerabilities_audit.remediation_strategy: Replace Command::output() with spawn() and register the Child handle in queue state (Arc<Mutex<Option<Child>>>); the worker polls try_wait() every ~150ms and, when the cancellation flag is set, calls child.kill() then wait(). Add a watchdog in pdf_engine.py (to_markdown in a worker thread with a configurable deadline; on timeout os._exit(EXIT_RUNTIME)) so even a non-killable upstream library cannot stall the queue. Also redirect engine stdout to a temp file instead of buffering the full markdown in RAM.

known_vulnerabilities_audit.root_cause_analysis: Demonstrated by real execution: pandoc GFM output for 'Shell var: `$PATH` and `$HOME`' is corrupted by the replace("$`","$")/replace("`$","$") heuristic into '$PATH` and $HOME`' - inline code spans are destroyed (opening backticks removed, trailing backtick left, unbalanced). Any document containing backtick-dollar adjacency (shell variables in inline code, PowerShell, template literals) is corrupted. The currency claim in the prompt is disproven: pandoc pre-escapes literal dollars (\$100 USD) so currency survives untouched. Secondary defect: any user fenced block whose info string is exactly 'math' (e.g., documentation about Markdown math) is force-converted to $$.
known_vulnerabilities_audit.architectural_impact: Silent content corruption of code spans in converted DOCX/TXT documents; the 'retain all formulas and special characters' contract is violated for code, and correctness depends on an unparseable string heuristic.
known_vulnerabilities_audit.remediation_strategy: AST-based fix: a pandoc Lua filter (--lua-filter) that rewrites Math elements to $...$/$$...$$ at AST level, leaving Text, Code, and CodeBlock elements untouched. If pandoc-side filtering is rejected, replace the string replace with a proper Markdown tokenizer that tracks fenced code blocks, indented code, and inline code spans and only rewrites delimiters outside code regions.

known_vulnerabilities_audit.root_cause_analysis: The specific backslash-claim is NOT reproducible in the current code: verified output uses forward slashes (![image](08_images/img_1.png)); pdf_engine relink builds f"{images_dir.name}/{name}" and pymupdf4llm md_path returns as_posix(). The vulnerability class ('un-normalized pathing in Markdown image links') IS present through a worse variant: pymupdf4llm 1.28.0 md_path replaces spaces with underscores in the markdown reference AND uses that sanitized string as the pix.save() target while the directory was created with the original name - deterministic FzErrorSystem code=2 hard failure for any output directory containing a space (verified for both absolute and relative paths, rc=4). md_path also depends on Path.cwd() via relative_to(), making engine output dependent on the process working directory.
known_vulnerabilities_audit.architectural_impact: Real users selecting folders like 'My Documents' get deterministic conversion failures for any PDF containing extractable images - a direct contradiction of the 0% crash claim. Backslash links themselves cannot occur in the current design.
known_vulnerabilities_audit.remediation_strategy: For backslashes: nothing to fix; add a regression test asserting no '\\' appears in emitted image links. For the space defect (see NEW_BUG_01): neutralize the path before invoking to_markdown - create both the real and the space-sanitized images directory, let pymupdf4llm write into the sanitized one, then relink/move files into the real directory and rewrite links from the actual on-disk files (the existing relink_images already does canonical renaming).

known_vulnerabilities_audit.root_cause_analysis: Measured: the six PDF fixtures extract to 306+559+85+197+130+223 = 1,500 characters combined - less than half a standard A4 page (~3,500 chars at 11pt). All PDFs are generated by the same toolchain (PyMuPDF insert_text), single built-in font (helv), no embedded fonts, no headers/footers, no margins, no vector art, no scanned pages, no OCR path. The 'math' fixture is ASCII text ('E = mc2'), not real typeset math. The 'Persian RTL' fixture contains ZERO Arabic codepoints (verified: text layer has none, output renders '···· ····'). The 'tables' fixture does produce genuine GFM tables (verified), but one 4x4 grid does not exercise table extraction at scale.
known_vulnerabilities_audit.architectural_impact: The '100% conversion success' claim is statistically void: the suite cannot detect regressions in RTL shaping, Unicode extraction, complex tables, scanned documents, or multi-page layouts. CI green provides no evidence of real-world robustness.
known_vulnerabilities_audit.remediation_strategy: Rebuild the suite with: multi-page fixtures (10-20 pages, 3,000-5,000 chars each), a real Arabic-script font with proper shaping (embedded font file, not 'tiro'), a scanned-photo PDF exercising the image/OCR path, real LaTeX typeset math, bordered/nested tables, mixed-script documents, and a statistical acceptance criterion (per-format character floor and verified non-Latin glyph counts asserted by codepoint ranges, not keyword matching).

newly_discovered_bugs.title: Output directory containing a space causes deterministic PDF image-extraction failure
newly_discovered_bugs.line_numbers: pdf_engine.py:109-118; pymupdf4llm utils.py md_path (space -> '_' replacement returned as the save path)
newly_discovered_bugs.root_cause_analysis: pymupdf4llm md_path replaces ' ' with '_' in the markdown reference and returns the sanitized string as the pix.save() filename, while images_dir.mkdir() creates the directory with the original space-containing name. pix.save then targets a non-existent directory -> FzErrorSystem code=2. Verified deterministic (4/4 runs failed) for both absolute and relative space paths; control runs without spaces succeeded. Output is also CWD-dependent via md_path's relative_to(Path.cwd()).
newly_discovered_bugs.failure_scenario: Any user selects an output directory with a space (e.g., 'C:/Users/Ahmad/Desktop/My Documents') and converts a PDF containing images: engine exits rc=4, item marked Failed. This is the most common Windows folder pattern.
newly_discovered_bugs.remediation_strategy: Pre-create the space-sanitized images directory before calling to_markdown (so pix.save succeeds), then reconcile: move files into the real <stem>_images/ directory and let relink_images rewrite links from actual disk files; additionally run the engine with a deterministic CWD or pass an absolute image_path so relative_to(Path.cwd()) cannot flip behavior.

newly_discovered_bugs.title: Persian RTL fixture contains zero Persian characters (silent font substitution)
newly_discovered_bugs.root_cause_analysis: Verified via pymupdf text-layer extraction: the fixture's text layer is 'Persian RTL Fixture... This fixture represents right-to-left scripts.... ···· ····' with 0 Arabic codepoints. 'tiro' is not a MuPDF built-in font; insert_text silently substituted a fallback that renders middle dots, and the except: pass swallows any real failure. The test suite therefore validates RTL extraction nowhere, yet reports 'persian_rtl_document' as a passing fixture.
newly_discovered_bugs.failure_scenario: Any regression in RTL/Unicode handling (e.g., bidi reordering, Arabic ligature extraction) ships undetected; phase reports claim 'success' for RTL coverage that does not exist.
newly_discovered_bugs.remediation_strategy: Embed a real Arabic-script font (e.g., Amiri) into the fixture document and assert the output contains codepoints in U+0600-U+06FF (range assertion, not string matching); remove the silent except or log the exception; verify glyph coverage at generation time.

newly_discovered_bugs.title: Browser mock assigns outputPath to unsupported files; native Rust returns null
newly_discovered_bugs.line_numbers: lines 75-98 (mockOutputPath applied to every file), tests/test_ipc_adapter.mjs lines 26-33 codify the divergence
newly_discovered_bugs.root_cause_analysis: Rust conversion.rs sets output_path: None (JSON null) for unsupported extensions (.jpg, .zip); the mock computes 'C:/output/photo.md' for photo.jpg. Any frontend logic that distinguishes unsupported items via outputPath===null will behave differently in browser preview vs native runtime.
newly_discovered_bugs.failure_scenario: A UI feature (e.g., 'Open output' disabled for unsupported files) works in dev preview and misbehaves in the packaged app, or vice versa.
newly_discovered_bugs.remediation_strategy: Mirror Rust semantics in mockStartBatch: outputPath = null when the extension is not in {pdf, docx, txt}; update the adapter test to assert the null contract.

newly_discovered_bugs.title: PDF engine has no time or resource bound (hang amplification + unbounded stdout buffering)
newly_discovered_bugs.root_cause_analysis: to_markdown runs in the main thread with no watchdog; a pathological PDF can loop indefinitely (observed class: md_path/pix.save cycles, decompression bombs). Separately, Command::output() buffers the entire child stdout in RAM, so a very large markdown output is fully materialized in memory before parsing.
newly_discovered_bugs.failure_scenario: A 500-page image-heavy PDF or crafted PDF hangs conversion for hours; memory grows with output size; cancel cannot help (see VULN_02).
newly_discovered_bugs.remediation_strategy: Run the conversion inside a bounded worker (thread with deadline; os._exit on timeout), stream engine stdout to a temp file rather than piped buffers, and cap pages/images with a documented limit that maps to a structured 'failed/skipped' result.

newly_discovered_bugs.title: Failed Pandoc runs can leave a partial output file on disk
newly_discovered_bugs.root_cause_analysis: Pandoc writes incrementally to --output; on a mid-run error the partial file stays on disk while Rust marks the item failed. Users see a failed item next to a half-written report.md, and a retry collides with the incremental-naming counter.
newly_discovered_bugs.failure_scenario: A truncated/corrupt DOCX makes pandoc exit non-zero after partially writing report.md; the stale partial file remains and report_1.md is generated on retry, confusing the output directory.
newly_discovered_bugs.remediation_strategy: Have Rust delete the output file when the subprocess exits non-zero, or write pandoc output to a temp name and atomically rename on success.

newly_discovered_bugs.title: phase_2_report.json artifact sizes are ambiguous between gate run and final delivery run
newly_discovered_bugs.root_cause_analysis: artifact_metadata_size_bytes=1774935 and executable_size_bytes=1803421 belong to engine gate run 31232120771, but the nested final_delivery_run (31234366171) omits its own sizes (actual artifact 1,775,373 bytes, exe 1,803,794 bytes). A reader can misattribute gate-run sizes to the final delivery.
newly_discovered_bugs.failure_scenario: Report consumers compare 'final' artifact size against the wrong value (373-byte metadata / 373-byte exe delta); metric audits of the delivery gate misread provenance.
newly_discovered_bugs.remediation_strategy: Nest per-run artifact metadata inside each run object and drop the generic top-level size fields (or label them 'engine_gate_run_artifact').

pass_1_pass_2_pass_3_flaw_free_modules: tool path resolution (Rust/Python parity, structured unavailable)
incremental filename sanitization (trailing dots/spaces, reserved names; verified Windows allows CON.md etc., sanitization is conservative-correct)
sequential worker lock discipline (no I/O under lock, poisoned-mutex tolerance)
pandoc Persian UTF-8 round-trip (16/16 Arabic codepoints preserved)
